title: Sennacherib
summary: Assyrian king in the Polyhistor extracts of Berossus (Cory 1876).
description: Added from the Cory import. Display only. Cory gives reign lengths and synchronisms, not a BC year this record can sort on, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Cory is display-only and gives none).

reign.note: pending CFAH reference (no CFAH anchor point or Table 1 entry found for this)

reign.date: “he reigned 18 years, and was cut off by a conspiracy”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 87; Berossus, ap. Alexander Polyhistor, ap. Eusebius
reign.note: Sinnecherim (Sennacherib), cut off by his son Ardu-Musanus. This is the first of two "18 years" in the edition.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 87; Berossus, ap. Alexander Polyhistor, ap. Eusebius
reign.note: The second "18 years", in the successors list. The two statements agree with each other.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 88; Berossus, ap. Alexander Polyhistor, ap. Eusebius
reign.note: From Sinecherim to Nabucodrossorus. Our check, not a figure of the text beyond the 88: 18 + 8 + 21 + 21 + 20 = 88, using the reigns printed from Sennacherib through Nabopolassar and not Nebuchadnezzar's 43. The 88 matches that sum.
